fixes.explanation: That's the third charge, friend. The council says they found this man "…proclaiming Himself to be Christ, a King." (Luke 23:2). It sits right next to the other two charges they bring to Pilate. Three accusations in one breath, all aimed at him.

That one doesn't show up in this list, friend. The council's last charge in Luke 23:2 is that He was "…proclaiming Himself to be Christ, a King." They also say He was subverting the nation and forbidding taxes to Caesar. Those are the accusations laid in front of Pilate.
Right, friend. Pilate does ask, "Are You the King of the Jews?" But Jesus doesn't deny it. He answers, "You have said so…" (Luke 23:3).
Pilate doesn't ask for more time, friend. He says plainly, "I find no basis for a charge against this man." (Luke 23:4). Those are his words to the chief priests and the crowds.
That's right, baker! Once Pilate learns Jesus is under Herod's jurisdiction, he sends Him to Herod (Luke 23:7). Herod himself was in Jerusalem at that time. Pilate passes Him along.

Caesar does come up, but only in the charges. The council said Jesus was forbidding payment of taxes to Caesar (Luke 23:2). When Pilate learns Jesus is under Herod's jurisdiction, he sends Him to Herod (Luke 23:7). Caesar isn't part of that trip.

Not that one, friend. Luke 23:7 says Pilate learns Jesus is under Herod's jurisdiction and sends Him to Herod. Pilate does say he finds no basis for a charge (Luke 23:4), but he doesn't send Him home. He passes Him along.
Yes, baker. Herod had heard about Jesus and was "…hoping to see Him perform a miracle." (Luke 23:8). He had wanted to see Him for a long time. When Herod saw Jesus, he was greatly pleased.

Right, baker. The chief priests and scribes do stand there, but Luke 23:10 says they were "…vehemently accusing Him." Nothing quiet about that. Meanwhile, Herod is questioning Jesus at great length (Luke 23:9).

That's it, baker. Luke 23:12 says, "That day Herod and Pilate became friends; before this time they had been enemies." Enemies one day and friends the same day. I think that's a strange way for a friendship to start.
Strangers isn't the word the text uses, friend. Luke 23:12 says "before this time they had been enemies." Then that very day they became friends.

Yes, baker. Pilate says he has examined Jesus in their presence and found Him "…not guilty of your charges against Him." (Luke 23:14). He's speaking to the chief priests, the rulers and the people he called together (Luke 23:13). He doesn't find Jesus guilty.
Yes, baker. Pilate says, "Therefore I will punish Him and release Him." (Luke 23:16). Release is the word he lands on. He says it again in Luke 23:22: "So after I punish Him, I will release Him."
Prison isn't in his plan, friend. Pilate says, "Therefore I will punish Him and release Him." (Luke 23:16). The word is release.
Question isn't part of that plan, friend. Pilate had already examined Jesus (Luke 23:14). His plan in Luke 23:16 is, "Therefore I will punish Him and release Him." The word he uses is release.

Yes, baker. Luke 23:19 says Barabbas "…had been imprisoned for an insurrection in the city, and for murder." It's a heavy detail, and the text puts it right there. That's the reason this man was in prison.

Blasphemy isn't what the text says about him, friend. Luke 23:19 says Barabbas "…had been imprisoned for an insurrection in the city, and for murder." It's a heavy part of the story. Murder is the other reason he was in prison.
That's what they shout, baker. Luke 23:21 says, "they kept shouting, 'Crucify Him! Crucify Him!'" Pilate wanted to release Jesus (Luke 23:20), and they kept shouting that instead.
Not what the text records, friend. In Luke 23:21 they "kept shouting, 'Crucify Him! Crucify Him!'" Pilate is trying to release Jesus, and that's the answer he gets back.
Banishing isn't mentioned, friend. Luke 23:21 says they "kept shouting, 'Crucify Him! Crucify Him!'" Pilate wants to release Jesus and that's what he's shouted back at.
That's right. Luke 23:23 says they were "…demanding with loud voices for Jesus to be crucified. And their clamor prevailed." Pilate said release over and over. In the end the noise won.

That's it, baker. Luke 23:24 says, "So Pilate sentenced that their demand be met." He had said again and again that he found no offense worthy of death. In the end, he gave them what they were demanding.
True, baker. Luke 23:25 says, "As they had requested, he released the one imprisoned for insurrection and murder…" That's Barabbas, and he's freed because of what they asked for.
It's true, friend. Luke 23:25 says, "As they had requested, he released the one imprisoned for insurrection and murder, and he handed Jesus over to their will." That's Barabbas going free.
